newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - May 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)

THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW China's most powerful economic minister and Vice-Premier Zhu Rongji is set to visit Australia with more than 70 top Chinese business leaders later this month. The visit confirms the success of Prime Minister John Howard's visit to Beijing early last month and reflects the improving diplomatic and commercial relations between the two countries. Page 1.

The Australian Manufacturing Workers Union says New South Wales is experiencing an average increase of 5.7 per cent in metal industry wages, well above the national average of 5.3 per cent. However, the sharp pace in wage increases in the State may be at an end, as two companies, Email and Southcorp Ltd, are fighting union attempts to gain a minimum pay benchmark of 10 per cent over two years. Page 3.

The Australian Democrats said yesterday they were preparing terms of reference for a Senate inquiry into Australia's media ownership rules, which could see key media owners, as well as Communications Minister Richard Alston, give evidence. The call comes as Federal Cabinet prepares to consider changes to the media ownership rules that may see Kerry Packer allowed to take over John Fairfax without selling his interests in the Nine Network. Page 3.

The Federal Management Committee of the National Party met via telephone hook-up last night, and is now expected to produce a set of specific amendments to Prime Minister John Howard's 10-point response to the High Court's Wik decision. The Nationals say the amendments are vital to avoid a split over the issue within the Coalition. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello and Coalition Senate Leader Robert Hill yesterday launched separate attacks on controversial Independent MP Pauline Hanson, accusing her of pushing a "divisive and vicious" plan for Australia and calling her newly formed One Nation party "dangerous". The comments clear the way for Prime Minister John Howard's first significant direct attack on Hanson, expected later this week. Page 1.

In an open letter to Prime Minister John Howard printed today, leading community figures and high-profile members of the Liberal party have called on the Federal Government to abandon his plan to relax media ownership rules in favour of media magnate Kerr Packer. The group called on Howard to stop any further concentration in media ownership, saying Australia cannot afford to have the media fall into fewer hands. Page 1.

In comments which come as the a new survey by Ernst and Young showed business was unhappy with the Federal Government's progress on tax reform, Treasurer Peter Costello said yesterday the main Federal Budget handout to encourage people to save would be more modest than Labor's "L.A.W" tax cuts plan, but would help more people, including retirees. Page 1.

In a move described by Australian Information Industry Association executive officer Peter Upton as "disappointing", Federal Defence Industry, Science and Personnel Minister Bronwyn Bishop is set to announce this week that the Department is awarding a five-year A$100 million information technology contract to an in-house team, casting doubt over the Coalition's outsourcing policy as a major part of its Budget strategy. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In comments which come as weekend fund-raising appearances by Independent MP Pauline Hanson sparked demonstrations and abuse between her supporters and critics, Federal Treasurer Peter Costello and the Government Leader in the Senate Robert Hill yesterday described Hanson's views as terrifying, divisive and vicious. Page 1.

Nearly 100 people gathered on the tiny New Zealand island of Rakino yesterday to mourn the death of Paula Brown, the Sydney hairdresser who was murdered one year ago. Brown's killer, or killers, have not yet been apprehended, but with five officers on the case full time, the police are confident they will be brought to justice. Page 1.

In a remarkable statement of where Sydney's sporting loyalties lie, yesterday's Australian Football League match between the Sydney Swans and Carlton attracted 40,623 supporters, while the four Australian Rugby League matches played between Friday night and yesterday afternoon attracted a combined attendance of just 36,369. Page 1.

As Federal Communication Minister Richard Alston prepares to take a proposal to dump existing media ownership laws and clear the way for Kerry Packer to make a takeover bid for the John Fairfax Holdings newspaper group to Cabinet in the next two days, more than 80 prominent Australians have joined forces to express their concern that the new changes will reduce the diversity and independence of the media. Page 1.
THE AGE

In an open letter to be published today, a group of prominent Australians - including former Prime Minister Malcolm Fraser, has called on the Federal Government not to allow media ownership in Australia to fall into fewer hands. The call comes as Federal Cabinet is due to consider tomorrow its review of the media ownership rules. Page A1.

The Poor Sisters of Nazareth Catholic religious order has launched an investigation into allegations that State wards were physically and emotionally abused at its Nazareth House home in Ballarat. The allegations include claims that young girls were beaten by nuns with sticks, canes and strips of rubber linoleum. Page A1.

Speaking at a media conference at Melbourne's A$2 billion Crown Casino on Saturday night, Crown chairman Lloyd Williams described himself as Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett's biggest fan and acknowledged the complex could not have been built without the support of the State Government. Page A1.

According to Marcus Clayton, a lawyer representing eight women who have made rape and sexual harassment allegations about police officers at Maryborough in Victoria, an 18-month internal investigation into the allegations is being thwarted by a loophole under the Police Regulation Act whereby officers can only be interviewed while on duty. Page A3.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
